title: The sharp degree bound for strong edge-colouring
decision_reason: Explicit source formulation, independent scholarly corroboration, fresh resolution and duplicate checks, separated A57 self-review and technical validation passed. No matching unresolved resolution claim was found.
aliases: Colouring the square of a line graph

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Every finite undirected loopless multigraph G with at least one edge; parallel edges are distinct edges.
problem_fingerprint.degree: Delta is the maximum vertex degree, counting multiplicity.
problem_fingerprint.constraint: A strong edge-colouring c:E(G)->{1,...,k} assigns different colours to distinct edges if they share an endpoint or some third edge shares an endpoint with each.
problem_fingerprint.observable: chi'_s(G), the least number of colours in such a colouring; an ordinary integral common-palette optimum.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: For every G, chi'_s(G)<=5 Delta^2/4 for even Delta, and chi'_s(G)<=(5 Delta^2-2 Delta+1)/4 for odd Delta.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: All finite sizes, degrees and loopless multigraphs; no bipartiteness, planarity, girth, sparsity, random-graph or sufficiently-large-degree assumption.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model: Existence only; no runtime guarantee, lists or fractional colour weights.
problem_fingerprint.equivalence: Proper vertex-colouring of L(G)^2, where distinct original edges are vertices of the simple line graph.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One underlying strong-edge-colouring family; no extra count for parity, a degree value, a restricted graph class, the simple-graph case or the square-line-graph formulation.

issues_found: Simple-graph shorthand would omit parallel edges explicitly included in the two full formulation sources.
The sharper odd-degree expression and original-graph degree must survive the line-graph reformulation.
Recent clique, higher-distance, cubic counterexample and finite-order claims can be confused with a resolution of the sharp colouring question.
Regularity reductions and fixed-forbidden-subgraph asymptotics need explicit scope checks.
The accompanying Lean dependency record lists project assumptions; a blanket claim of independent formal verification would be unsupported.
issues_resolved: Retained the source multigraph conventions and a direct edge-conflict definition; checked extremal constructions at both parities.
Compared the full relevant theorem/model statements in the eleven-source ledger; separated ten scope comparisons from discovery-only items.
Checked regular completion, dependence of the K_{t,t}-free threshold on fixed t, clique-versus-colouring and worst-case-versus-random quantifiers.
Disclosed the artifact's certificate and literature assumptions and that its code was not rerun.
Repeated repository alias/formula searches, reread complete nearest entries 344 and 348, and checked current remote main.
second_review.application_check: Frequency or slot assignment is an exact interpretation of the stated graph conflicts. No physical propagation model or efficient algorithm is promised.

hypothesis_comparison: Finite loopless multigraphs, maximum degree four.
The conclusion allows 21 colours.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The target at degree four is 20. Simplicity arising later for a minimal counterexample does not restrict the theorem's original multigraph scope or sharpen its constant.

hypothesis_comparison: The stated upper bound is 1.772 Delta^2.
A sufficiently-large-degree threshold is required.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The coefficient exceeds 5/4 and the theorem is not an all-degree sharp bound. No multigraph extension is assumed in this comparison.

hypothesis_comparison: Reported coefficient 1.73, for sufficiently large degree.
Regular graphs are completed from arbitrary graphs without raising the original maximum degree.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The regularity reduction removes regularity, not the gap in coefficient or degree threshold. Even granting the reported bound, it does not give the target.

hypothesis_comparison: Bipartite upper bounds retain large-degree hypotheses and coefficients above the bipartite target.
The random theorem fixes edge density in (0,1), bounds the part-size ratio, and holds asymptotically almost surely.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: These hypotheses do not cover every finite graph. A high-probability assertion cannot rule out worst-case counterexamples; no bipartite-to-arbitrary transfer giving the sharp bound was identified.

resolution_comparisons.theorem_locator: Theorem 1.2 and its following biregular reduction
hypothesis_comparison: Bipartite input with side maxima Delta_A and Delta_B both sufficiently large.
Conclusion permits 1.676 Delta_A Delta_B.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Biregular completion preserves a bipartite restriction. It neither covers arbitrary nonbipartite graphs nor yields the exact sharp constant.

hypothesis_comparison: Simple cubic bipartite graphs of arbitrarily large girth.
The construction needs more than five colours.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: This disproves a separate five-colour proposal. The current conjecture permits ten colours at degree three; the counterexample does not contradict it.

hypothesis_comparison: Finite simple graphs; the observable is omega(L(G)^2).
The Ore-degree theorem concerns a bipartite subgraph whose edges form a clique.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: An upper bound on clique number does not upper-bound chromatic number in general. The reported 2607/1987 coefficient also exceeds 5/4; neither conclusion supplies a strong colouring.

hypothesis_comparison: h_t restricts to graphs whose entire t-th line-graph power is complete.
The new counterexamples concern t=3 and a cubic-in-degree proposal; the older t=2 edge-count theorem is separately stated.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: These address a different distance or a restricted complete-conflict case. The solved h_2 statement does not partition arbitrary edge sets into colour classes.

hypothesis_comparison: Fixed epsilon>0 and fixed integer t>=2.
Input excludes K_{t,t} as a subgraph; the degree threshold depends on epsilon and t.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Choosing t larger than the input degree does not provide a uniform threshold independent of t. C5 blow-ups contain large bicliques. The fixed-t result does not resolve the unrestricted conjecture.

hypothesis_comparison: Formalized headlines have the same nonsharp coefficients or random/bipartite restrictions.
The general SEC row explicitly lists project-specific certificate assumptions and an external colouring theorem.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The artifact is not a separate proof of the sharp conjecture, and the listed dependencies are disclosed rather than described as independently certified. No code was rerun.

independently_authored_corroboration.reason: Both author sets are disjoint from the original formulation paper. HSY18 restates the parity-sensitive multigraph problem; C26's July 2026 Conjecture 28 and surrounding discussion retain the sharp question.
independently_authored_corroboration.scope: Exact parity and multigraph conventions come from full FSGT90/HSY18 text; the current survey and 2026 primary progress papers corroborate continued study of the unresolved sharp bound. Different versions of any one work count only once.

nearest_existing.distinction: Arbitrary edge-specific colour lists with only shared-endpoint conflicts; asks for equality with the ordinary chromatic index. The new question has a common palette, distance-two conflicts and a sharp degree bound.

A vertex-colouring bound in the degree and clique number of the graph being coloured. Substitution H=L(G)^2 does not turn its right-hand side into the required expression in Delta(G); no logical independence is asserted.

normalization_checks: Every pair of parallel edges shares endpoints and must receive distinct colours. Degree counts their multiplicity; loops are excluded as in the source conventions.

The line graph is simple even for a multigraph: each original edge is a separate vertex. The conflict rule is adjacency at line-graph distance one or two, not an ambiguous endpoint-distance convention.
The bound uses the original graph's maximum degree. Integral common-palette colouring, arbitrary finite input and no runtime constraint are retained.
For odd Delta=2s+1, the five part sizes s+1,s+1,s,s,s give 5s^2+4s+1 edges and maximum degree 2s+1; for even Delta the balanced construction gives 5 Delta^2/4. Delta=1 is immediate.
Both proposed expressions are integers at their respective parity. No floor, ceiling, hidden asymptotic slack or sufficiently-large-degree condition is inserted.
Applying the broad Reed inequality to a line-graph square with only general degree/clique estimates leaves slack; the formulations are not equivalent.
The application is exact only for the stated graph interference rule. It promises neither a physical SINR model nor a polynomial-time construction.
